components.note: 氵 (water) — liquids and flowing; 没 first meant sink or submerge (淹没), which led to "gone" and then "not have".
殳 (shū) is only a loose sound hint for 没 (méi/mò); it also sits in 设 shè and 投 tóu.
穴 (cave) — 穴 is a cave or hole, as in 窗 window, 穷 poor; 空 is empty like a hollow.
工 (gōng) — near sound — 空 is kōng; also in 红 hóng.

example.hanzi: 我今天没空，我们改天再聊吧。
example.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān méi kòng, wǒmen gǎitiān zài liáo ba.
example.english: I don't have time today; let's talk another day.
example.fact: Switzerland's national rail operator, SBB, runs one of the most punctual networks in the world, with roughly 90% of trains arriving within three minutes of schedule — a feat achieved partly because the entire national timetable is coordinated to the minute across every connecting line.

examples.hanzi: 今晚我没空,下次一起吃饭吧。
examples.pinyin: Jīnwǎn wǒ méi kòng, xià cì yìqǐ chīfàn ba.
examples.english: I'm not free tonight; let's have dinner together next time.

examples.hanzi: 他最近太忙,连吃饭都没空。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuìjìn tài máng, lián chīfàn dōu méi kòng.
examples.english: He's so busy lately that he doesn't even have time to eat.

components.note: 争 (contend) — simplified from 爭, two hands pulling at the same object. See 战争 war and 竞争 compete.
扌 (hand) — hand radical — 执 is to hold or grasp, then carry out, as in 执行.

example.hanzi: 两位邻居因为停车位发生了争执。
example.pinyin: Liǎng wèi línjū yīnwèi tíngchēwèi fāshēng le zhēngzhí.
example.english: The two neighbors got into a dispute over a parking spot.
example.fact: Bir Tawil, a roughly 2,060-square-kilometer patch of desert between Egypt and Sudan, is one of the few pieces of land on Earth that no country claims — both nations disavow it because claiming it would mean giving up their claim to the more valuable, disputed Hala'ib Triangle nearby.

examples.hanzi: 他们因为钱的事发生了争执。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen yīnwèi qián de shì fāshēngle zhēngzhí.
examples.english: They had a dispute over money.

examples.hanzi: 别为这点小事争执,伤了感情。
examples.pinyin: Bié wèi zhè diǎn xiǎoshì zhēngzhí, shāngle gǎnqíng.
examples.english: Don't argue over such a small thing and hurt your relationship.

components.note: 彳 (step, 双人旁) — walking along a path, as in 行 go, 往 toward; 循 is to follow a route.
盾 (dùn) is only a loose sound clue for xún.
王 (jade) — 王 on the left is 玉 (jade) as in 玩, 球, 现; 环 is a jade ring, as in 环境.

example.hanzi: 水在自然界中不断循环。
example.pinyin: Shuǐ zài zìránjiè zhōng bùduàn xúnhuán.
example.english: Water continuously cycles through nature.
example.fact: A single water molecule spends an average of about nine days in Earth's atmosphere before falling back down as precipitation, but it can remain locked in polar ice sheets or deep groundwater for thousands of years. The same water molecules cycling through today's rain have likely been recycled through the atmosphere and oceans countless times since the planet's oceans formed.

examples.hanzi: 血液在身体里循环。
examples.pinyin: Xuèyè zài shēntǐ lǐ xúnhuán.
examples.english: Blood circulates in the body.

examples.hanzi: 这首歌我一直单曲循环,听了一整天。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shǒu gē wǒ yìzhí dānqǔ xúnhuán, tīngle yì zhěngtiān.
examples.english: I've had this song on repeat all day.

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
日 (sun) — time and day, as in 时, 晚, 明: the sun at the top of a sprout, early morning. 早 also gives 草 cǎo and 澡 zǎo.

example.hanzi: 他一早就出发去机场了。
example.pinyin: Tā yīzǎo jiù chūfā qù jīchǎng le.
example.english: He set off for the airport early in the morning.
example.fact: Benjamin Franklin was a famous early riser who claimed to wake at 5 a.m. and outlined an idealized daily schedule in his autobiography. Modern chronobiology research, however, shows that a person's natural sleep-wake preference is largely genetic, so 'morning lark' versus 'night owl' tendencies are not simply a matter of willpower.

examples.hanzi: 我一早起来就去跑步了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yìzǎo qǐlái jiù qù pǎobù le.
examples.english: I got up early in the morning and went running.

examples.hanzi: 明天一早我们就要出发。
examples.pinyin: Míngtiān yìzǎo wǒmen jiù yào chūfā.
examples.english: We have to set off first thing tomorrow morning.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 推; 探 is to reach out and feel, then to explore.
The right half is a sound part shared with 深 shēn: a loose clue for tàn.
糸 (thread, traditional of 纟) — silk and cord: 紧 tight, 系 tie; 索 is a twisted rope, seen in 线索 clue.

example.hanzi: 科学家们不断探索宇宙的奥秘。
example.pinyin: Kēxuéjiāmen bùduàn tànsuǒ yǔzhòu de àomì.
example.english: Scientists continually explore the mysteries of the universe.
example.fact: Voyager 1, launched by NASA in 1977, is now the most distant human-made object from Earth, having crossed into interstellar space in 2012. It is currently more than 24 billion kilometers away and still transmits data back to Earth, though its plutonium power source is expected to run too low to operate any instruments by around 2025.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们喜欢探索新的地方。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen xǐhuan tànsuǒ xīn de dìfang.
examples.english: Children like to explore new places.

examples.hanzi: 他一生都在探索如何让人们生活得更好。
examples.pinyin: Tā yìshēng dōu zài tànsuǒ rúhé ràng rénmen shēnghuó de gèng hǎo.
examples.english: He spent his life exploring how to make people's lives better.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 停 is a person stopping.
亭 (tíng) sounds exactly like 停; same part in 婷 tíng.
手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.

example.hanzi: 裁判喊了一声，两名拳手立刻停手。
example.pinyin: Cáipàn hǎn le yī shēng, liǎng míng quánshǒu lìkè tíngshǒu.
example.english: The referee shouted, and the two boxers stopped immediately.
example.fact: In professional boxing, a referee can stop a fight through a technical knockout even without a boxer being knocked down, if they are deemed unable to safely continue. The mechanism was formalized in the early 20th century after several in-ring deaths pushed boxing commissions to give referees stronger authority to halt dangerous or mismatched bouts.

examples.hanzi: 我一喊停,你们就停手,不要再吵了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yì hǎn tíng, nǐmen jiù tíngshǒu, bú yào zài chǎo le.
examples.english: When I call stop, you stop; no more arguing.

examples.hanzi: 他一再劝我,我才停手不干了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yízài quàn wǒ, wǒ cái tíngshǒu bú gàn le.
examples.english: He kept urging me, and only then did I stop doing it.

components.note: 马 (horse) — horses and riding, as in 骑 ride, 驾 drive, 驴 donkey.
区 (qū) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 躯 qū.
辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads, as in 道 road, 追 chase.
豕 (pig) — the oldest form shows a foot chasing a pig, hence to pursue.

example.hanzi: 那个国家驱逐了一批外国记者。
example.pinyin: Nàge guójiā qūzhú le yī pī wàiguó jìzhě.
example.english: That country expelled a group of foreign journalists.
example.fact: In 1609, Spain expelled hundreds of thousands of Moriscos — Muslims who had converted to Christianity — in one of the largest forced population movements in early modern European history, reshaping the demographics of entire regions of southern Spain within just a few years.

examples.hanzi: 因为违反了规定,他被驱逐出境。
examples.pinyin: Yīnwèi wéifǎnle guīdìng, tā bèi qūzhú chūjìng.
examples.english: He was deported for violating the rules.

examples.hanzi: 老师把捣乱的同学驱逐出了教室。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī bǎ dǎoluàn de tóngxué qūzhú chūle jiàoshì.
examples.english: The teacher kicked the disruptive student out of the classroom.

components.note: 疒 (illness, 病字旁) — sickness and pain: 疼 ache, 痛 pain, 瘦 thin; here the word for illness itself.
丙 (bǐng) is a near sound match for bìng; also in 柄 bǐng handle.
户 (door) — doors and houses, as in 所 and 扇: a room with a door.
方 (fāng) is a close sound clue for fáng; 方 also sounds out 放 fàng and 访 fǎng.

example.hanzi: 护士每小时都会来病房检查病人。
example.pinyin: Hùshi měi xiǎoshí dōu huì lái bìngfáng jiǎnchá bìngrén.
example.english: The nurse comes to the ward to check on patients every hour.
example.fact: Florence Nightingale's statistical work during the Crimean War in the 1850s showed that far more soldiers were dying of preventable infections in unsanitary hospital wards than of battle wounds. Her push for cleaner facilities and better ventilation helped found the modern field of hospital epidemiology.

examples.hanzi: 奶奶住在三楼的病房,我每天去看她。
examples.pinyin: Nǎinai zhù zài sān lóu de bìngfáng, wǒ měitiān qù kàn tā.
examples.english: Grandma is in a ward on the third floor, and I visit her every day.

examples.hanzi: 病房里很安静,病人都在休息。
examples.pinyin: Bìngfáng lǐ hěn ānjìng, bìngrén dōu zài xiūxi.
examples.english: It's quiet in the ward, and the patients are all resting.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
衣 (clothes) — a picture of a coat with a collar and sleeves. As a radical it is 衤 on the left: 裤 trousers, 衬 shirt, 被 quilt.

example.hanzi: 天气变冷了，她穿上了厚厚的大衣。
example.pinyin: Tiānqì biàn lěng le, tā chuān shàng le hòuhòu de dàyī.
example.english: The weather turned cold, so she put on a thick overcoat.
example.fact: Merino sheep wool fibers are naturally crimped and can absorb roughly 30% of their weight in moisture while still keeping the wearer feeling dry, which is why wool coats and base layers remain effective insulators for polar explorers even in freezing, humid conditions where synthetic fabrics can fail.

examples.hanzi: 冬天我喜欢穿一件长长的黑色大衣。
examples.pinyin: Dōngtiān wǒ xǐhuan chuān yí jiàn chángcháng de hēisè dàyī.
examples.english: In winter I like to wear a long black overcoat.

examples.hanzi: 这件大衣有点薄,不够暖和。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn dàyī yǒudiǎn báo, bú gòu nuǎnhuo.
examples.english: This coat is a bit thin and isn't warm enough.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 付 is handing 寸 something to a person.
付 (fù) is also the sound in 附 fù, 府 fǔ, 符 fú and 腐 fǔ.
纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 线, 组; 给 is to supply thread, then to give.
合 (hé) is only a loose sound clue; same part in 答 dá, 拾 shí, 恰 qià.

example.hanzi: 公司每月按时把工资付给员工。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī měi yuè ànshí bǎ gōngzī fùgěi yuángōng.
example.english: The company pays employees' salaries on time every month.
example.fact: Some of the oldest surviving payroll records come from ancient Mesopotamia, where workers building temples and canals around 3000 BC were paid in rations of barley beer. A typical laborer received about two liters a day, with the amount recorded on cuneiform tablets scaling with rank, similar to a modern pay grade.

examples.hanzi: 我已经付给他两百块钱了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǐjīng fùgěi tā liǎng bǎi kuài qián le.
examples.english: I've already paid him two hundred yuan.

examples.hanzi: 这笔钱应该付给谁?
examples.pinyin: Zhè bǐ qián yīnggāi fùgěi shéi?
examples.english: Who should this money be paid to?

components.note: 尺 (ruler) — the main part, as in 尺寸 size. Dictionary story: a place where measures are discussed (口), like a bureau; 局 also means 'game' as in 结局.
口 (mouth/box) — placed inside 尺. It represents talk or a space; Memory aid: a ruler fitted to a mouth means rules are discussed in an 'office'.
力 (strength) — 力 is strength, as in 办, 动, 努; 势 is force or momentum.

example.hanzi: 分析师密切关注着国际局势的变化。
example.pinyin: Fēnxīshī mìqiè guānzhù zhe guójì júshì de biànhuà.
example.english: Analysts are closely watching changes in the international situation.
example.fact: During the 1962 Cuban Missile Crisis, the world came arguably closer to nuclear war than at any other point in history. Declassified records later revealed that Soviet submarine officer Vasili Arkhipov was one of three men required to authorize a nuclear torpedo launch and was the lone dissenting vote that prevented it.

examples.hanzi: 目前的局势很紧张,大家都很担心。
examples.pinyin: Mùqián de júshì hěn jǐnzhāng, dàjiā dōu hěn dānxīn.
examples.english: The current situation is tense, and everyone is worried.

examples.hanzi: 比赛的局势一下子变了,我们领先了。
examples.pinyin: Bǐsài de júshì yíxiàzi biàn le, wǒmen lǐngxiān le.
examples.english: The situation in the game suddenly changed and we took the lead.

components.note: 车 (chariot) — war chariots drawn up in a circle (the top part shows the enclosure): an army camp, hence military.
士 (scholar, soldier) — usually read as an axe or weapon, so a warrior or gentleman (士兵, 博士). Memory aid: 士 has the longer bar on top, 土 (earth) on the bottom.

example.hanzi: 那位军士负责训练新兵。
example.pinyin: Nà wèi jūnshì fùzé xùnliàn xīnbīng.
example.english: That noncommissioned officer is in charge of training new recruits.
example.fact: The rank structure separating commissioned officers from noncommissioned officers dates back to the Roman legions, where centurions — promoted from the ranks rather than appointed by birth or political connection — commanded roughly 80 soldiers each and were prized for battlefield experience rather than social standing.

examples.hanzi: 这位老军士教过很多新兵。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi lǎo jūnshì jiàoguo hěn duō xīnbīng.
examples.english: This veteran sergeant has trained many recruits.

examples.hanzi: 军士长命令大家集合。
examples.pinyin: Jūnshìzhǎng mìnglìng dàjiā jíhé.
examples.english: The sergeant major ordered everyone to assemble.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and liquids, as in 河, 海, 汤: clear water.
青 (qīng) gives the exact sound; also 请 qǐng, 情 qíng, 晴 qíng and 精 jīng.
氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海; 洗 is to wash.
先 (xiān) — near sound — 洗 is xǐ; 先 also sounds out 选 xuǎn.

example.hanzi: 医生反复叮嘱要用肥皂彻底清洗双手。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng fǎnfù dīngzhǔ yào yòng féizào chèdǐ qīngxǐ shuāngshǒu.
example.english: The doctor repeatedly reminded people to thoroughly wash their hands with soap.
example.fact: In the 1840s, Hungarian physician Ignaz Semmelweis discovered that hospital deaths from childbed fever dropped dramatically when doctors washed their hands with a chlorinated lime solution before examining patients. His idea was rejected by most of his medical peers during his lifetime, and it took decades for handwashing to become standard medical practice.

examples.hanzi: 吃水果以前,先用清水清洗一下。
examples.pinyin: Chī shuǐguǒ yǐqián, xiān yòng qīngshuǐ qīngxǐ yíxià.
examples.english: Before eating fruit, rinse it with clean water first.

examples.hanzi: 他每个周末都清洗自己的汽车。
examples.pinyin: Tā měi gè zhōumò dōu qīngxǐ zìjǐ de qìchē.
examples.english: He washes his car every weekend.

meanings: woman of senior authority in a household

components.note: 主 (master, host) — a lamp with a flame on top; a lamp stand was the centre of the room. 主 also sounds out 注 zhù, 住 zhù and 柱 zhù.
女 (woman) — 女 marks women, as in 妈, 姐; 妇 is a married woman.
彐 (hand) — 彐 is a hand holding a broom (the traditional 婦 had 帚), so a married woman who keeps house.

example.hanzi: 她是一位全职主妇，把家里打理得井井有条。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yī wèi quánzhí zhǔfù, bǎ jiā lǐ dǎlǐ de jǐngjǐngyǒutiáo.
example.english: She is a full-time housewife who keeps the household perfectly organized.
example.fact: Economists who try to estimate the market value of unpaid household work — cooking, cleaning, and childcare — have found it would add trillions of dollars a year to major economies if it were counted in GDP. OECD estimates put the value of unpaid household work at roughly 20 to 60 percent of measured GDP, depending on the country.

examples.hanzi: 我妈妈是一位家庭主妇,每天忙着做家务。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ māma shì yí wèi jiātíng zhǔfù, měitiān mángzhe zuò jiāwù.
examples.english: My mom is a housewife and is busy with housework every day.

examples.hanzi: 这位主妇每天都去菜市场买菜。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi zhǔfù měitiān dōu qù càishìchǎng mǎi cài.
examples.english: This housewife goes to the market to buy groceries every day.

components.note: 贝 (shell, money) — 贝 is money, as in 买, 费, 贵; 财 is wealth.
才 (cái) — same sound — 财 is cái, like 才; 才 also sounds out 材 cái.
力 (strength) — effort, as in 办, 助, 努: tasks take effort. The top 夂 stands in for the traditional 務.

example.hanzi: 她负责公司的财务工作。
example.pinyin: Tā fùzé gōngsī de cáiwù gōngzuò.
example.english: She is in charge of the company's financial affairs.
example.fact: Double-entry bookkeeping, the accounting method still used by virtually every modern business, was first systematically described in 1494 by Italian friar and mathematician Luca Pacioli in a mathematics textbook, centuries before accounting became a distinct profession.

examples.hanzi: 他在一家大公司负责财务。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yì jiā dà gōngsī fùzé cáiwù.
examples.english: He is in charge of finance at a large company.

examples.hanzi: 公司的财务状况越来越好。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī de cáiwù zhuàngkuàng yuè lái yuè hǎo.
examples.english: The company's financial situation is getting better and better.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — plants; 菜 is vegetables, as in 草 grass, 花 flower.
采 (cǎi) is the same syllable with a different tone; it also sounds out 彩 cǎi and 踩 cǎi.
单 (dān) gives sound to 弹 dàn/tán and 蝉 chán; as a word it means single, alone, a list.

example.hanzi: 服务员递给我们一份菜单。
example.pinyin: Fúwùyuán dì gěi wǒmen yī fèn càidān.
example.english: The waiter handed us a menu.
example.fact: The printed restaurant menu is often traced to Paris in the years after the French Revolution, when many chefs who had cooked for aristocratic households lost their positions and opened public restaurants, listing dishes and prices on paper for a general paying clientele for the first time.

examples.hanzi: 我们先看看菜单,再决定点什么。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xiān kànkan càidān, zài juédìng diǎn shénme.
examples.english: Let's look at the menu first and then decide what to order.

examples.hanzi: 这家餐厅的菜单是中英文的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de càidān shì Zhōng-Yīngwén de.
examples.english: This restaurant's menu is in both Chinese and English.

components.note: Memory aid: 业 looks like a row of upright posts on a base, like a shop sign or an old tool stand; 'business/trade' is the extended meaning. Origin is unclear, so no firm etymology.
力 (strength) — effort, as in 办, 助, 努: tasks take effort. The top 夂 stands in for the traditional 務.

example.hanzi: 这家银行的业务范围很广。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā yínháng de yèwù fànwéi hěn guǎng.
example.english: This bank's scope of business is very broad.
example.fact: Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena, founded in Siena, Italy in 1472, is recognized as the world's oldest bank still in operation, having survived plagues, wars, and multiple financial crises across more than five centuries of continuous business.

examples.hanzi: 他们公司的主要业务是出口茶叶。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen gōngsī de zhǔyào yèwù shì chūkǒu cháyè.
examples.english: Their company's main business is exporting tea.

examples.hanzi: 他刚来,对业务还不太熟悉。
examples.pinyin: Tā gāng lái, duì yèwù hái bú tài shúxī.
examples.english: He just arrived and isn't very familiar with the work yet.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快, 忙, 情: a strange feeling.
圣 here is not the "sage" word; it is only a loose sound clue for guài.
⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — the body-part radical, as in 脸, 腿, 脑; 胎 is a fetus, and by extension a tyre.
台 (tái) gives the sound exactly: 胎 tāi is close.

example.hanzi: 那部电影里的怪胎其实心地善良。
example.pinyin: Nà bù diànyǐng lǐ de guàitāi qíshí xīndì shànliáng.
example.english: The "freak" character in that movie is actually kind-hearted.
example.fact: Conjoined twins occur in roughly one out of every 200,000 live births and result when a single fertilized egg only partially separates into two embryos during early development, typically between the 13th and 15th day after conception — a narrow window that determines whether, and how much, the twins remain joined.

examples.hanzi: 同学们都叫他怪胎,因为他的想法很特别。
examples.pinyin: Tóngxuémen dōu jiào tā guàitāi, yīnwèi tā de xiǎngfǎ hěn tèbié.
examples.english: His classmates call him a weirdo because his ideas are unusual.

examples.hanzi: 在这个小镇上,大家都觉得他是个怪胎。
examples.pinyin: Zài zhège xiǎozhèn shàng, dàjiā dōu juéde tā shì gè guàitāi.
examples.english: In this small town, everyone thinks he's a freak.

components.note: 页 (head, page) — heads and faces: 头, 额 forehead, 题 title, 领 collar; 顺 is a head following the river 川 along.
川 (chuān) is only a loose sound hint; 训 xùn and 顺 shùn share it.
广 (building) — 广 is a building or wide roof, as in 店 shop, 床 bed, 库 store; 序 is order and sequence.
予 (yǔ) — near sound — 序 is xù; 予 also sounds out 预 yù and 野 yě.

example.hanzi: 请按照字母顺序排列这些名字。
example.pinyin: Qǐng ànzhào zìmǔ shùnxù páiliè zhèxiē míngzi.
example.english: Please arrange these names in alphabetical order.
example.fact: Alphabetical ordering as an organizing principle dates back at least to the Library of Alexandria in the 3rd century BC, where librarian Callimachus is credited with cataloguing works by author name in alphabetical sequence — one of the earliest known uses of the system still used in dictionaries and indexes today.

examples.hanzi: 请你按顺序排队,不要插队。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ àn shùnxù páiduì, bú yào chāduì.
examples.english: Please line up in order and don't cut in line.

examples.hanzi: 这几个步骤的顺序不能弄错。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jǐ gè bùzhòu de shùnxù bù néng nòng cuò.
examples.english: The order of these steps can't be mixed up.

components.note: 木 (wood) — trees; 柠 is the lemon tree, as in 树 tree, 林 forest.
宁 (níng) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 拧 níng and 狞 níng.
木 (wood) — trees; 檬 appears in 柠檬 lemon, as in 树 tree, 林 forest.
蒙 (méng) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 朦 méng.

example.hanzi: 她在茶里加了一片柠檬。
example.pinyin: Tā zài chá lǐ jiā le yī piàn níngméng.
example.english: She added a slice of lemon to her tea.
example.fact: In 1747, Scottish naval surgeon James Lind conducted one of the first controlled clinical trials in medical history, showing that sailors who ate citrus fruits like lemons and oranges recovered from scurvy far faster than those given other remedies — decades before vitamin C was even identified as the active ingredient.

examples.hanzi: 我喜欢在水里放几片柠檬。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan zài shuǐ lǐ fàng jǐ piàn níngméng.
examples.english: I like to put a few slices of lemon in my water.

examples.hanzi: 这杯柠檬汁太酸了,我想加点糖。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bēi níngméng zhī tài suān le, wǒ xiǎng jiā diǎn táng.
examples.english: This lemon juice is too sour, so I'd like to add some sugar.

components.note: 自 (self) — picture of a nose; Chinese speakers point to the nose to mean "I", so it became "self" (compare 鼻 bí, nose, which adds 畀).
身 (body) — a person's body with a rounded belly. As a radical it marks body words: 躺 lie down, 躲 hide, 躯 body.

example.hanzi: 公司必须先解决自身的问题才能扩张。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī bìxū xiān jiějué zìshēn de wèntí cáinéng kuòzhāng.
example.english: The company must first solve its own problems before it can expand.
example.fact: The human body replaces the vast majority of its cells on a regular cycle — red blood cells last about four months, skin cells shed and regenerate roughly every two to four weeks — so most of the atoms making up a person's body today were not part of it a decade ago, even though a sense of continuous selfhood persists.

examples.hanzi: 我们应该先解决自身的问题。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yīnggāi xiān jiějué zìshēn de wèntí.
examples.english: We should first solve our own problems.

examples.hanzi: 这件事与他自身的努力分不开。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì yǔ tā zìshēn de nǔlì fēn bù kāi.
examples.english: This has everything to do with his own effort.

components.note: 山 (mountain) — a gorge lies between mountains; also in 峰 peak, 岛 island.
夹 (jiā) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 狭 xiá and 侠 xiá.
谷 — water (八) flowing out of a valley mouth (口). It also sounds out 浴 yù, 欲 yù and 俗 sú.

example.hanzi: 他们徒步穿越了那条壮观的峡谷。
example.pinyin: Tāmen túbù chuānyuè le nà tiáo zhuàngguān de xiágǔ.
example.english: They hiked through that spectacular canyon.
example.fact: The Grand Canyon in Arizona is roughly 446 kilometers long and up to 1,857 meters deep, carved almost entirely by the Colorado River over the past five to six million years — a geologically short time span that has exposed nearly two billion years of Earth's rock layers along its walls.

examples.hanzi: 我们坐船穿过了这条深深的峡谷。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zuò chuán chuānguòle zhè tiáo shēnshēn de xiágǔ.
examples.english: We took a boat through this deep canyon.

examples.hanzi: 峡谷两边都是高高的岩石。
examples.pinyin: Xiágǔ liǎngbiān dōu shì gāogāo de yánshí.
examples.english: Both sides of the canyon are tall rock walls.

components.note: 肉 — a picture of a slab of meat with its grain lines; as a left-hand radical it shrinks to ⺼ in 脸, 腿, 肌.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 体 is a person's body.
本 (root) — the root of a person, the body; the traditional form was 體 with 骨 (bone).

example.hanzi: 长期缺乏运动会让肉体变得虚弱。
example.pinyin: Chángqī quēfá yùndòng huì ràng ròutǐ biàn de xūruò.
example.english: Long-term lack of exercise can make the physical body weak.
example.fact: Astronauts on long-duration missions can lose up to 20% of their muscle mass and significant bone density within just a few months in microgravity, since muscles and bones no longer have to work against gravity — which is why ISS crew members exercise roughly two hours a day using specialized resistance equipment.

examples.hanzi: 运动不但锻炼肉体,也能放松心情。
examples.pinyin: Yùndòng búdàn duànliàn ròutǐ, yě néng fàngsōng xīnqíng.
examples.english: Exercise trains the body and also relaxes the mind.

examples.hanzi: 人的肉体会老,但精神可以一直年轻。
examples.pinyin: Rén de ròutǐ huì lǎo, dàn jīngshén kěyǐ yìzhí niánqīng.
examples.english: The body ages, but the spirit can stay young.

meanings: (of celestial bodies etc) to move along one's course
(of a train service etc) to operate

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 运 is to move, then to be moved by luck.
云 (yún) is a near sound match for yùn.
彳 (step) — left half of a crossroads: 行 pictures a crossroads, so to go, and (háng) a row or trade.

example.hanzi: 这条地铁线路每天早上五点开始运行。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo dìtiě xiànlù měitiān zǎoshàng wǔ diǎn kāishǐ yùnxíng.
example.english: This subway line starts operating at 5 a.m. every day.
example.fact: The London Underground, which opened in 1863, is the world's oldest underground railway system and initially ran on steam-powered locomotives through tunnels filled with smoke and soot, decades before electric trains were introduced on the network in the 1890s.

examples.hanzi: 这台机器已经连续运行了一整天。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tái jīqì yǐjīng liánxù yùnxíngle yì zhěngtiān.
examples.english: This machine has been running continuously for a whole day.

examples.hanzi: 电脑运行得太慢,我想重启一下。
examples.pinyin: Diànnǎo yùnxíng de tài màn, wǒ xiǎng chóngqǐ yíxià.
examples.english: The computer is running too slowly, so I want to restart it.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 运 is to move, then to be moved by luck.
云 (yún) is a near sound match for yùn.
车 (vehicle) — carrying by cart; also in 轮 wheel, 辆 for cars.
俞 (yú) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 愉 yú and 愈 yù.

example.hanzi: 这些货物需要用大型卡车运输。
example.pinyin: Zhèxiē huòwù xūyào yòng dàxíng kǎchē yùnshū.
example.english: These goods need to be transported by large trucks.
example.fact: The modern steel shipping container, standardized globally in the 1960s, is often credited with cutting the cost of international trade so dramatically that it reshaped the world economy — loading a ship went from days of manual labor per port call to just hours with cranes, letting a single large container ship now carry the equivalent of over 20,000 truckloads of cargo.

examples.hanzi: 这批水果用火车运输,三天后到。
examples.pinyin: Zhè pī shuǐguǒ yòng huǒchē yùnshū, sān tiān hòu dào.
examples.english: This batch of fruit is shipped by train and arrives in three days.

examples.hanzi: 他在一家运输公司当司机。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yì jiā yùnshū gōngsī dāng sījī.
examples.english: He works as a driver at a transport company.

components.note: 豸 (beast) — 豸 is an animal or beast radical, as in 豹; 貌 is appearance.
皃 (mào) — same sound — 貌 is mào, like 皃.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 像 resemble; 似 is to look like.
以 (yǐ) is only a loose sound hint for sì.

example.hanzi: 这道题貌似很简单，其实暗藏陷阱。
example.pinyin: Zhè dào tí màosì hěn jiǎndān, qíshí àncáng xiànjǐng.
example.english: This problem appears to be simple, but it actually hides a trap.
example.fact: The mimic octopus, discovered off Indonesia in the 1990s, can impersonate the appearance and movement of more than a dozen other sea creatures — including venomous lionfish and sea snakes — by changing its shape, color, and swimming pattern, likely to deter predators that avoid those more dangerous animals.

examples.hanzi: 他貌似很高兴,其实心里很难过。
examples.pinyin: Tā màosì hěn gāoxìng, qíshí xīnlǐ hěn nánguò.
examples.english: He seems happy, but in fact he feels sad.

examples.hanzi: 这个人貌似我以前见过。
examples.pinyin: Zhège rén màosì wǒ yǐqián jiànguo.
examples.english: This person looks like someone I've met before.

components.note: 夕 (evening, night) — night and time: 外, 多, 夜; dreams come at night, so 夕 is the meaning clue; 林 is only filler.
见 (see) — a big eye on a person's legs 儿: a person looking. The same 见 is in 现 appear, 觉 sense, 视 look.

example.hanzi: 昨晚我梦见自己在天上飞。
example.pinyin: Zuówǎn wǒ mèngjiàn zìjǐ zài tiān shàng fēi.
example.english: Last night I dreamed I was flying through the sky.
example.fact: Most vivid dreaming occurs during REM sleep, a stage discovered in 1953 by researchers at the University of Chicago who noticed rapid eye movements and irregular brain activity in sleeping subjects. The body also becomes almost completely paralyzed during REM sleep, a state called atonia thought to prevent people from physically acting out their dreams.

examples.hanzi: 我小时候梦见自己会飞,太有意思了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎoshíhou mèngjiàn zìjǐ huì fēi, tài yǒu yìsi le.
examples.english: When I was little I dreamed I could fly, which was so fun.

examples.hanzi: 昨天我梦见了已经去世的爷爷。
examples.pinyin: Zuótiān wǒ mèngjiànle yǐjīng qùshì de yéye.
examples.english: Yesterday I dreamed about my late grandfather.

components.note: 纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord words: 红 red, 给 give, 线 line; a thread has an end, which fits 终 end.
冬 (dōng) rhymes with 终 zhōng, and 冬 originally meant the end (of the year) too — so it helps sound and sense.
止 (stop) — a picture of a foot planted on the ground: where the foot stops. Seen in 步 step (two feet) and 正 correct.

example.hanzi: 双方决定终止这项合作协议。
example.pinyin: Shuāngfāng juédìng zhōngzhǐ zhè xiàng hézuò xiéyì.
example.english: Both parties decided to terminate the cooperation agreement.
example.fact: NASA's Space Shuttle program was officially terminated in 2011 after 135 missions over 30 years, following the loss of two orbiters — Challenger in 1986 and Columbia in 2003 — with the decision driven partly by the high cost of extending the aging fleet's certified service life.

examples.hanzi: 由于下雨,活动被迫终止了。
examples.pinyin: Yóuyú xiàyǔ, huódòng bèi pò zhōngzhǐ le.
examples.english: Because of the rain, the event had to be called off.

examples.hanzi: 如果对方违约,你可以终止合同。
examples.pinyin: Rúguǒ duìfāng wéiyuē, nǐ kěyǐ zhōngzhǐ hétong.
examples.english: If the other party breaks the contract, you can terminate it.

components.note: 木 (wood) — trees and wooden things: 树, 板, 样; 模 was a wooden mold or pattern.
莫 (mò) is close to mó; same part in 摸 mō, 膜 mó, 墓 mù.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 桌 table, 板 board; 样 once meant a tree (acorn) and later "form, pattern".
羊 (yáng, sheep) is a near-exact sound clue for yàng; 羊 also sounds out 洋 yáng and 养 yǎng.

example.hanzi: 多年不见，他的模样几乎没变。
example.pinyin: Duō nián bù jiàn, tā de múyàng jīhū méi biàn.
example.english: After many years apart, his appearance has barely changed.
example.fact: Researchers who study facial aging have found that the human face keeps its recognizable proportions for decades mainly because bone structure changes little after growth stops around age 20. Most visible aging comes instead from soft-tissue and skin changes — fat redistribution, collagen loss, and gravity's gradual pull — rather than the skeleton reshaping itself.

examples.hanzi: 这孩子的模样很像他爸爸。
examples.pinyin: Zhè háizi de móyàng hěn xiàng tā bàba.
examples.english: This child looks a lot like his dad.

examples.hanzi: 他装出一副可怜的模样,想骗我给他买玩具。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhuāngchū yí fù kělián de móyàng, xiǎng piàn wǒ gěi tā mǎi wánjù.
examples.english: He put on a pitiful look, hoping to trick me into buying him a toy.

meanings: (of a document etc) to be uploaded to the Internet
(tennis, volleyball etc) to move in close to the net

components.note: 上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.
网 (net) — a picture of a hanging net with crossing cords; as a radical it appears as 罒 in 罚, 置, 罗.

example.hanzi: 现在几乎每个人每天都要上网。
example.pinyin: Xiànzài jīhū měi gèrén měitiān dōu yào shàngwǎng.
example.english: Nowadays almost everyone goes online every day.
example.fact: The first message ever sent over what became the Internet was transmitted in 1969 between computers at UCLA and Stanford Research Institute. The system crashed after just two letters of the word "login" were typed, making "lo" the accidental first message in internet history.

examples.hanzi: 我一般晚上上网看新闻。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yìbān wǎnshang shàngwǎng kàn xīnwén.
examples.english: I usually go online to read the news in the evening.

examples.hanzi: 这里可以免费上网吗?
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ kěyǐ miǎnfèi shàngwǎng ma?
examples.english: Can I get online here for free?

meanings: China north of the Yellow River

components.note: 北 — two people (匕) back to back; the meaning "north" is a later loan, and "back" survives in the reading bèi (败北 defeat).
方 (square, direction) — early picture is disputed (a plough-like tool or lashed boats). Sound clue in 房 fáng, 防 fáng, 访 fǎng, 放 fàng.
亠 (lid) — the top. Memory aid: a lid over a bent shape — a square-cornered 'side' or place, as in 地方, 方法.

example.hanzi: 冬天北方常常大雪纷飞。
example.pinyin: Dōngtiān běifāng chángcháng dàxuě fēnfēi.
example.english: In winter, heavy snow often falls in the north.
example.fact: Earth's magnetic north pole is not fixed — it has been drifting from northern Canada toward Siberia at speeds that increased to roughly 50 to 60 kilometers per year in recent decades, forcing scientists to update the World Magnetic Model used by compasses, ships, and smartphone navigation more frequently than planned.

examples.hanzi: 我老家在北方,冬天特别冷。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ lǎojiā zài běifāng, dōngtiān tèbié lěng.
examples.english: My hometown is in the north, and winters are especially cold.

examples.hanzi: 北方人爱吃饺子和面条。
examples.pinyin: Běifāng rén ài chī jiǎozi hé miàntiáo.
examples.english: Northerners love eating dumplings and noodles.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — plants; 葡 is the grape plant, as in 草 grass, 花 flower.
匍 (pú) gives the exact sound.
艹 (grass) — plants; 萄 is part of 葡萄 grape, as in 草 grass, 花 flower.
匋 (táo) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 陶 táo and 淘 táo.
酉 (wine jar) — fermented drinks and flavors: 醉 drunk, 醒 sober, 酸 sour, 配 match; 酒 is liquor, with 氵 for the liquid.
酉 also hints at the sound: yǒu is close to jiǔ.

example.hanzi: 晚餐时他们开了一瓶红葡萄酒。
example.pinyin: Wǎncān shí tāmen kāi le yī píng hóng pútáojiǔ.
example.english: They opened a bottle of red wine at dinner.
example.fact: Archaeologists have found chemical residue of wine in pottery jars from the Republic of Georgia dating back roughly 8,000 years, making it some of the earliest evidence of winemaking yet discovered — long before wine culture became associated with ancient Greece and Rome.

examples.hanzi: 他们在庆祝会上喝了几杯葡萄酒。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zài qìngzhùhuì shàng hēle jǐ bēi pútáojiǔ.
examples.english: They had a few glasses of wine at the celebration.

examples.hanzi: 这瓶葡萄酒是用法国的葡萄酿的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè píng pútáojiǔ shì yòng Fǎguó de pútáo niàng de.
examples.english: This bottle of wine is made from French grapes.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — cutting, as in 到, 分, 别: 制 is cutting to shape, then to make and to control.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家 home, 安 safe, 客 guest; settling down under a roof.
正 (zhèng, upright; the lower part is written 疋) is a loose sound clue for dìng; also in 证 zhèng and 政 zhèng.

example.hanzi: 政府正在制定新的环保政策。
example.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ zhèngzài zhìdìng xīn de huánbǎo zhèngcè.
example.english: The government is drawing up a new environmental policy.
example.fact: The 1987 Montreal Protocol, an international treaty drawn up to phase out ozone-depleting chemicals like CFCs, is considered one of the most successful environmental agreements ever ratified — it achieved universal ratification by all 198 UN member states, and the Antarctic ozone hole has been slowly shrinking as a result.

examples.hanzi: 学校正在制定新的作息时间表。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào zhèngzài zhìdìng xīn de zuòxī shíjiānbiǎo.
examples.english: The school is drawing up a new daily schedule.

examples.hanzi: 我给自己制定了一个学习计划。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gěi zìjǐ zhìdìngle yí gè xuéxí jìhuà.
examples.english: I made myself a study plan.

components.note: 刂 (knife, 立刀旁) — cutting and peeling, as in 别, 刻, 剪.
录 (lù) is only a loose clue; it also sounds out 绿 lǜ and 碌 lù.

example.hanzi: 请帮我剥一个橙子。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ bāo yí gè chéngzi.
example.english: Please peel an orange for me.
example.fact: 剥 has two readings: bāo is the colloquial 'peel, shell' (剥虾 shell prawns); bō is literary, found in 剥削 (exploit) and 剥夺 (deprive).

examples.hanzi: 她给孩子剥了一个鸡蛋。
examples.pinyin: Tā gěi háizi bāo le yí ge jīdàn.
examples.english: She peeled an egg for the child.

examples.hanzi: 你会不会剥虾壳？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ huì bu huì bāo xiākér?
examples.english: Do you know how to shell shrimp?

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical — 仪 is the conduct of a person, as in 仪式 ceremony.
义 (yì) — near sound — 仪 is yí; 义 also sounds out 议 yì.

example.hanzi: 这个仪式很重要。
example.pinyin: Zhège yíshì hěn zhòngyào.
example.english: This ceremony is very important.
example.fact: 仪 is a bound form: 仪式 (ceremony), 礼仪 (etiquette), 仪器 (instrument), 仪表 (appearance; also a gauge). Anything named 某某仪 is typically a measuring device, as in 地球仪 (globe).

examples.hanzi: 婚礼的司仪讲得很风趣。
examples.pinyin: Hūnlǐ de sīyí jiǎng de hěn fēngqù.
examples.english: The wedding host spoke in a very humorous way.

examples.hanzi: 医生用仪器检查他的心脏。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng yòng yíqì jiǎnchá tā de xīnzàng.
examples.english: The doctor checked his heart with an instrument.

components.note: 犭 (animal) — 犭 is the animal radical, as in 猫, 狗, 狼; 猴 is a monkey.
侯 (hóu) — same sound — 猴 is hóu, like 侯; 侯 also sounds out 喉 hóu and 候 hòu.

example.hanzi: 动物园里有很多猴子。
example.pinyin: Dòngwùyuán lǐ yǒu hěn duō hóuzi.
example.english: There are lots of monkeys at the zoo.
example.fact: The monkey is the ninth zodiac animal (猴年 = year of the monkey) and the star of Journey to the West as 美猴王, the Monkey King. The measure word is 只.

examples.hanzi: 那只小猴子特别调皮。
examples.pinyin: Nà zhī xiǎo hóuzi tèbié tiáopí.
examples.english: That little monkey is especially naughty.

examples.hanzi: 我弟弟是属猴的。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ dìdi shì shǔ hóu de.
examples.english: He was born in the Year of the Monkey.

components.note: 灬 (fire) — marks fire and cooking, as in 煮 boil, 蒸 steam; 熏 is smoking or fumigating over a fire.

example.hanzi: 这种肉是用烟熏的。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng ròu shì yòng yān xūn de.
example.english: This meat is smoked.
example.fact: 熏 covers smoking food (熏肉, 熏鱼), fumigating (熏蚊子) and being irritated by smoke. In 熏陶 (to influence gradually) it may also be written 薰陶.

examples.hanzi: 这种茶叶是用花熏出来的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng cháyè shì yòng huā xūn chūlái de.
examples.english: This tea is scented with flowers.

examples.hanzi: 厨房里的烟把我熏得直流泪。
examples.pinyin: Chúfáng lǐ de yān bǎ wǒ xūn de zhí liúlèi.
examples.english: The smoke in the kitchen made my eyes water.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 枪 first meant a wooden spear; wood radical also in 棍 stick and 板 board.
仓 (cāng) hints at the sound — close to qiāng; the same part is in 抢 qiǎng and 苍 cāng.
聲 (traditional) — a hanging stone chime struck, with 耳 (ear) below: a sound you hear. 声 keeps only the top, so the picture is mostly lost.
士 (scholar) — the top of 声 is only a leftover of the old chime, not 'scholar'. Do not read meaning into it.

example.hanzi: 深夜里突然传来一声枪声。
example.pinyin: Shēnyè lǐ tūrán chuánlái yī shēng qiāngshēng.
example.english: A gunshot suddenly rang out in the dead of night.
example.fact: A gunshot's characteristic crack is partly a sonic boom: many bullets travel faster than the speed of sound (about 343 meters per second at sea level), so the sharp noise people hear is a small shockwave, distinct from and often louder than the muzzle blast of the gun itself.

examples.hanzi: 他听到了枪声,马上趴在了地上。
examples.pinyin: Tā tīngdàole qiāngshēng, mǎshàng pā zàile dìshang.
examples.english: He heard a gunshot and immediately dropped to the ground.

examples.hanzi: 电影里传来一阵枪声,大家都很紧张。
examples.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ chuánlái yí zhèn qiāngshēng, dàjiā dōu hěn jǐnzhāng.
examples.english: A burst of gunfire came from the movie, and everyone tensed up.

components.note: 生 (to grow) — old forms of 青 show fresh growing plants plus pigment; the colour is fresh blue-green. 青 also sounds out 清, 请, 情, 晴.
年 (year) — first drawn as a person carrying harvested grain: one harvest per year. Seen in 今年, 去年, 年轻.

example.hanzi: 越来越多的青年选择自主创业。
example.pinyin: Yuèláiyuè duō de qīngnián xuǎnzé zìzhǔ chuàngyè.
example.english: More and more young people are choosing to start their own businesses.
example.fact: The United Nations defines "youth" as people aged 15 to 24, a group that numbered around 1.2 billion people globally as of the early 2020s — roughly one in every six people on the planet — with the largest concentrations of young people found in Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia.

examples.hanzi: 这位青年每天坚持学习外语。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi qīngnián měitiān jiānchí xuéxí wàiyǔ.
examples.english: This young man keeps studying foreign languages every day.

examples.hanzi: 青年人应该多读书、多运动。
examples.pinyin: Qīngniánrén yīnggāi duō dúshū, duō yùndòng.
examples.english: Young people should read more and exercise more.

components.note: 止 (foot) — a foot heading straight for a target line: upright, correct. 正 gives sound to 证 zhèng, 整 zhěng and 政 zhèng.
目 (eye) — sighting along a straight line. 直 also sounds out 值 zhí and 植 zhí.

example.hanzi: 大家都很信任他，因为他为人正直。
example.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu hěn xìnrèn tā, yīnwèi tā wéirén zhèngzhí.
example.english: Everyone trusts him because he is an honest and upright person.
example.fact: A 2019 study published in Science dropped over 17,000 "lost" wallets containing varying amounts of cash in more than 40 countries and found that people were, on average, more likely to report and return a wallet containing money than one without — a result that surprised even the researchers who ran the experiment.

examples.hanzi: 做人要正直,不能说谎。
examples.pinyin: Zuòrén yào zhèngzhí, bù néng shuōhuǎng.
examples.english: You should be honest and not lie.

examples.hanzi: 他是个正直的警察,从不收礼。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì gè zhèngzhí de jǐngchá, cóng bù shōu lǐ.
examples.english: He's an upright police officer who never accepts gifts.

components.note: 专 (zhuān) also gives its sound to 转 zhuǎn, 传 chuán, 砖 zhuān and 团 tuán (traditional 專).
氵 (water) — water and pouring, as in 河, 海, 清: 注 is to pour in.
主 (zhǔ) is a close sound clue for zhù; 主 also in 住 zhù, 柱 zhù and 驻 zhù.

example.hanzi: 她工作时非常专注，很少被打扰。
example.pinyin: Tā gōngzuò shí fēicháng zhuānzhù, hěn shǎo bèi dǎrǎo.
example.english: She is extremely focused when working and is rarely disturbed.
example.fact: Psychologist Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi coined the term "flow" in the 1970s to describe the state of deep, focused absorption in a task where a person loses track of time. His research found that flow is most likely to occur when a task's difficulty closely matches a person's skill level — too easy causes boredom, too hard causes anxiety.

examples.hanzi: 上课要专注,不要看手机。
examples.pinyin: Shàngkè yào zhuānzhù, bú yào kàn shǒujī.
examples.english: Concentrate in class and don't look at your phone.

examples.hanzi: 孩子专注地看着小鱼在水里游来游去。
examples.pinyin: Háizi zhuānzhù de kànzhe xiǎoyú zài shuǐ lǐ yóu lái yóu qù.
examples.english: The child watched the little fish swimming around, completely absorbed.

components.note: 凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.
走 (walk, run) — a person with swinging arms above a foot 止. As a radical it marks movement: 起, 越, 超, 趣.

example.hanzi: 他十六岁离家出走，独自在城市里生活了三年。
example.pinyin: tā shíliù suì lí jiā chūzǒu, dúzì zài chéngshì lǐ shēnghuóle sān nián.
example.english: He left home at sixteen and lived alone in the city for three years.
example.fact: Young wolves dispersing from their birth pack have been GPS-tracked traveling over 800 kilometers in search of new territory, one of the longest recorded journeys of any land mammal leaving home. Most dispersers travel alone, and researchers in the northern Rockies have found their survival rate is far lower than for wolves that stay with the pack.

examples.hanzi: 他一气之下出走了，家人找了他一整夜。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīqì zhī xià chūzǒu le, jiārén zhǎo le tā yī zhěng yè.
examples.english: He stormed off in anger, and his family searched for him all night.

examples.hanzi: 这位国王被迫出走，再也没有回到故乡。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi guówáng bèipò chūzǒu, zài yě méiyǒu huídào gùxiāng.
examples.english: The king was forced into exile and never returned home.

components.note: 癶 (two feet) — two feet stepping upward: 登 is to climb or board, as in 登山 mountain-climbing.
豆 (dòu) is only a loose sound hint; 登 dēng also sounds out 灯 dēng and 凳 dèng.
阝 (mound, 左耳旁 on the left) — land and hills, as in 院, 阳, 队. The right part is a simplification with no sound clue.

example.hanzi: 1969年，阿波罗11号成功登陆月球表面。
example.pinyin: yī jiǔ liù jiǔ nián, Ābōluó shíyī hào chénggōng dēnglù yuèqiú biǎomiàn.
example.english: In 1969, Apollo 11 successfully landed on the surface of the moon.
example.fact: The Apollo 11 lunar module touched down with less than 30 seconds of fuel remaining, after Neil Armstrong had to manually steer past a boulder field to a safer landing site. The onboard guidance computer had only about 4KB of RAM, far less processing power than a modern digital watch.

examples.hanzi: 台风预计明天凌晨登陆沿海地区。
examples.pinyin: Táifēng yùjì míngtiān língchén dēnglù yánhǎi dìqū.
examples.english: The typhoon is expected to make landfall on the coast early tomorrow.

examples.hanzi: 这款手机下个月将登陆中国市场。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuǎn shǒujī xià gè yuè jiāng dēnglù Zhōngguó shìchǎng.
examples.english: This phone will be launched in the Chinese market next month.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — organs and body parts, as in 肺 lung, 胃 stomach, 脑 brain.
干 (gān) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 竿 gān and 杆 gǎn.
⺼ (flesh, form of 月) — body parts: 脑, 脚, 肚; 脏 is an organ (zàng), and also dirty (zāng).
庄 (zhuāng) is a near sound match for zàng/zāng; also in 装 zhuāng.

example.hanzi: 肝脏是人体内最大的内脏器官，负责分解毒素。
example.pinyin: gānzàng shì réntǐ nèi zuì dà de nèizàng qìguān, fùzé fēnjiě dúsù.
example.english: The liver is the largest internal organ in the human body, responsible for breaking down toxins.
example.fact: The human liver has remarkable regenerative power — surgeons can remove up to 70 percent of it for a living-donor transplant, and the remaining tissue regrows to nearly its original size within a few months. This is one of the few organs in the body capable of that kind of regrowth.

examples.hanzi: 喝太多酒会伤害肝脏。
examples.pinyin: Hē tài duō jiǔ huì shānghài gānzàng.
examples.english: Drinking too much alcohol damages the liver.

examples.hanzi: 医生说他的肝脏有点问题，需要做进一步检查。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng shuō tā de gānzàng yǒudiǎn wèntí, xūyào zuò jìnyībù jiǎnchá.
examples.english: The doctor said there is a problem with his liver and he needs further tests.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 改, 放: to gather by force or hand.
丩 (jiū) is only a loose sound clue for shōu.
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: to grip or rely on.
居 (jū) is a close sound clue for jù; 居 also in 剧 jù and 锯 jù.

example.hanzi: 请保留好这张收据，退货时需要用到。
example.pinyin: qǐng bǎoliú hǎo zhè zhāng shōujù, tuìhuò shí xūyào yòngdào.
example.english: Please keep this receipt, you'll need it if you return the item.
example.fact: Paper receipts printed on thermal paper often contain bisphenol A (BPA), a chemical that can transfer to skin on contact, which is part of why many large retailers have switched to BPA-free paper or digital receipts. Sweden was among the first countries to require that all point-of-sale receipts be offered digitally by law.

examples.hanzi: 你付款以后，店员会给你一张收据。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ fùkuǎn yǐhòu, diànyuán huì gěi nǐ yī zhāng shōujù.
examples.english: After you pay, the clerk will give you a receipt.

examples.hanzi: 我把收据弄丢了，还能退货吗？
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ shōujù nòngdiū le, hái néng tuìhuò ma?
examples.english: I lost the receipt. Can I still return it?

components.note: 口 (mouth) — holding something in the mouth; also in 吃 eat, 吞 swallow.
今 (jīn) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 贪 tān and 琴 qín.
义 (justice, meaning) also lends its sound to 议 yì discuss, 仪 yí ceremony and 蚁 yǐ ant — a useful clue in many characters.

example.hanzi: 这首诗的含义比表面看起来复杂得多。
example.pinyin: zhè shǒu shī de hányì bǐ biǎomiàn kàn qǐlái fùzá de duō.
example.english: The meaning of this poem is much more complex than it appears on the surface.
example.fact: The Rosetta Stone carries the same decree in three scripts — hieroglyphic, Demotic, and Greek — and it was the parallel Greek text that finally let scholars unlock the meaning of Egyptian hieroglyphs after they had been unreadable for over a thousand years. Jean-François Champollion completed the decipherment in 1822.

examples.hanzi: 这个词在不同的场合有不同的含义。
examples.pinyin: Zhège cí zài bùtóng de chǎnghé yǒu bùtóng de hányì.
examples.english: This word has different meanings in different situations.

examples.hanzi: 你能解释一下这句话的含义吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng jiěshì yīxià zhè jù huà de hányì ma?
examples.english: Can you explain what this sentence means?

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical — 传 is something passed from person to person.
专 (zhuān) — near sound — 传 is chuán; 专 also sounds out 转 zhuǎn and 砖 zhuān.
言 (speech) — 言 is the traditional full form of the 讠 radical for speech and language: 说, 话, 语, 请.

example.hanzi: 网上流传的那个传言后来被证实是假的。
example.pinyin: wǎngshàng liúchuán de nàge chuányán hòulái bèi zhèngshí shì jiǎ de.
example.english: The rumor that spread online was later proven to be false.
example.fact: Psychologist Gordon Allport's 1947 research on rumor transmission found that details of a story tend to sharpen and simplify with each retelling, a distortion process called 'leveling and sharpening.' It is the same mechanism that lets a small kernel of truth snowball into a wildly exaggerated rumor.

examples.hanzi: 传言说公司下个月要裁员。
examples.pinyin: Chuányán shuō gōngsī xià gè yuè yào cáiyuán.
examples.english: Rumor has it the company will lay off staff next month.

examples.hanzi: 别相信那些没有根据的传言。
examples.pinyin: Bié xiāngxìn nàxiē méiyǒu gēnjù de chuányán.
examples.english: Don't believe those groundless rumors.

components.note: 页 (head) — marks the head and face, as in 顶 top, 题 topic, 额 forehead; 频 pairs it with repeating motion for 'again and again'.
幺 (tiny thread) — the dictionary story is a cord pulled taut in a frame, so 'to lead'; another account sees a bird net. Origin is disputed.
十 (ten) — the lower bar. Reads shuài to lead (率领) and lǜ for rate (效率, 比率). Memory aid: ten threads pulled together as a rate.

example.hanzi: 调整收音机的频率才能收听到这个电台。
example.pinyin: tiáozhěng shōuyīnjī de pínlǜ cáinéng shōutīng dào zhège diàntái.
example.english: You have to adjust the radio's frequency to pick up this station.
example.fact: Human ears can typically detect sound frequencies between about 20 Hz and 20,000 Hz, but that range narrows with age — many adults over 50 lose the ability to hear anything above 12,000-15,000 Hz. Elephants, by contrast, communicate using infrasound frequencies as low as 5 Hz, below human hearing, which can travel for kilometers through the ground.

examples.hanzi: 他每周去健身房的频率很高。
examples.pinyin: Tā měi zhōu qù jiànshēnfáng de pínlǜ hěn gāo.
examples.english: He goes to the gym very frequently every week.

examples.hanzi: 这种鸟的叫声频率很高，人耳几乎听不到。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng niǎo de jiàoshēng pínlǜ hěn gāo, rén ěr jīhū tīng bù dào.
examples.english: This bird's call is so high in frequency that human ears can barely hear it.

components.note: 手 (hand) — over 目 (eye): a hand shading the eyes to look into the distance. 目 marks seeing words, as in 眼, 睡.
宀 (roof) — a house or shelter, as in 家 home, 安 safe, 完; a hand 寸 under a roof means guarding.
寸 (hand, inch) — originally a hand, as in 对, 寻, 封.

example.hanzi: 两名警卫日夜看守着博物馆的大门。
example.pinyin: liǎng míng jǐngwèi rìyè kānshǒu zhe bówùguǎn de dàmén.
example.english: Two guards watch over the museum's entrance day and night.
example.fact: The Terracotta Army, buried over 2,200 years ago to guard Emperor Qin Shi Huang's tomb, consists of more than 8,000 life-sized soldiers, each with individually sculpted facial features — no two faces are exactly alike, suggesting the craftsmen may have used real soldiers as models.

examples.hanzi: 他在仓库里看守了一整夜。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài cāngkù lǐ kānshǒu le yī zhěng yè.
examples.english: He kept watch over the warehouse all night.

examples.hanzi: 牧羊人一直看守着山坡上的羊群。
examples.pinyin: Mùyángrén yīzhí kānshǒu zhe shānpō shàng de yángqún.
examples.english: The shepherd kept watching over the flock on the hillside.

components.note: 贝 (cowry shell, money) — wealth and trade: 财, 费, 买; 资 is capital or resources.
次 (cì) is a loose clue; same part in 姿 zī and 咨 zī.
力 (strength) — effort, as in 办, 男, 努; 助 is to lend strength.
且 (qiě) is a loose sound clue for zhù; 且 also sounds out 祖 zǔ, 租 zū and 姐 jiě.

example.hanzi: 这项研究得到了政府的大力资助。
example.pinyin: zhè xiàng yánjiū dédào le zhèngfǔ de dàlì zīzhù.
example.english: This research received substantial funding from the government.
example.fact: The Manhattan Project, the U.S. program that developed the first nuclear weapons during World War II, was subsidized with roughly $2 billion (about $30 billion in today's dollars) and at its peak employed over 130,000 people across sites most of them didn't know were connected.

examples.hanzi: 一位企业家资助了这个孩子上大学。
examples.pinyin: Yī wèi qǐyèjiā zīzhù le zhège háizi shàng dàxué.
examples.english: An entrepreneur funded this child's university education.

examples.hanzi: 这个项目需要有人资助才能继续下去。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiàngmù xūyào yǒurén zīzhù cáinéng jìxù xiàqù.
examples.english: This project needs someone to fund it before it can continue.
